_about: Men in the water: release 2's sailor rules (Brian, 22 November 12:49Z, 'Do all of these'; the design director's form ruling 12:58Z, the oil narrowed at 17:39Z and the figures ruled at 17:42Z). Every figure is the historian's record (historian/sailors-record-1122.md) as the design director ruled it, and none is tuned. The field reads nothing here unless a battle's ticket carries 'sailors' (the switch, off as shipped). It covers what a lost ship puts in the water, who goes down with her, how long men live in the sea, and when and by whom they are picked up. Who wins never reads any of it.

down._about: The share of a ship's crew that goes down with her, by how she went (the design director, 17:42Z, S1 and S2). 'sudden' is a destroyer sunk by a torpedo salvo or from the air, by torpedo or bomb (the design director, 19:15Z: Hammann, Jarvis and Sims, historian-destroyer-sudden-cases-1122.md): 42%, Hammann's share, the one case that reads apart from the water, since ships picked up her men at once; whether a ship stood by is the pick-up's and the water's, never this share's. Sims (about 92%, 16 found on day 4) and Jarvis (100%, alone) are marks for the whole chain, read after the build and never a knob. The field has no magazine and books a loss at the blow, so it cannot see a big ship go in under five minutes. Big-ship sudden (Hood, Juneau, Barham) waits for a field magazine (the after-release list). Every other loss is 'fought': slow, with her men fighting for her, 25% (Indianapolis, Repulse, Prince of Wales, Wasp, Lexington). 'early' is a ship whose men left her early, in good order: 1% (Ark Royal; Lexington's abandonment).

dead._about: Men killed going into the water whose bodies float (sea:men's 'dead'). None until the record gives a figure (S3): the shares above already count the men the hits killed.

alive._about: The share of the men who went into the water still alive after so many hours in it, by the water's band (the historian's table by sea and month: 'water'), with straight lines between the record's points (S5). Cold and temperate water leave none alive past their last point (48 hours). Warm water runs on to Indianapolis's 35% at 100 hours. The rules read it no further than 96 hours past the fight's end. 'arctic' is water under 4 C (the design director, 18:50Z, from the historian's section 4b: men in life jackets with no raft, 85% at 15 minutes, 60% at 30, 20% at an hour, 5% at an hour and a half, none at three), read only in the sea-months the historian lays as arctic ('a') in the water table.

found._about: Hours after the fight's end (S6). A side holding the water that stops for survivors picks up every man still alive at 'stop' (the record's 1 to 2 hours, its middle). The men of a side that leaves them, or that no one stops for, are found at 'leave' (the cases' middle: Glorious 3 days, Indianapolis 4, Juneau 8).

pick._about: Men a minute that each ship of a piece the player has stopped at a wreck takes aboard in the fight (S7, the historian's D; Dorsetshire's 1.4 a minute or more fits a cruiser), every class: 'wreck' from a ship that went down fighting, 'early' from one whose men left her in good order.

refuse._about: Navies whose men in the water refuse an enemy's pick-up (S8: Vella Gulf, one battle, recorded so). None of them become prisoners: they are lost unless their own side holds the water. The one sourced navy row; every other rule is one for every navy.

oil._about: Every wreck leaves a slick at her place. It burns only where a carrier went down to a torpedo salvo or to aircraft (the design director, 17:39Z: the record's oil fires are carriers and tankers sunk by torpedo or bomb, and the field has no tankers). The record gives no radius, burn time or toll, so burning oil takes no man and delays no pick-up: the rules say only whether it burns. 'r' and 'burn' are KNOBS, LOOKS ONLY, PROPOSED by the naval rules thread on 22 November for the design director to rule: the slick's spread by class in metres, and how long a carrier's burns in seconds, for the 3D scene to draw (sea:oil). Nothing in the rules reads them.

abandon._about: How long a ship her men abandoned stays afloat before her sinking is told (sea:sunk, and her slick): a KNOB, LOOKS ONLY, PROPOSED by the naval rules thread on 22 November for the design director to rule, at the 3D sea scene's ask (17:52Z: 180 seconds at least for her boats to get clear, 240 if the fight allows; the record's abandoned ships stayed afloat for hours: Ark Royal 14, Lexington and Yorktown longer). The rules book her lost when her men leave her; only the telling waits, and an action that ends sooner tells it at its end.

water._about: The sea's band by month, January first: a arctic (under 4 C, only where the historian lays it), c cold (under 10 C), t temperate (10 to 21 C), w warm (over 21 C). The historian's table (historian/sailors-record-1122.md, section 5), by the campaign's sea ids.
